texts.preamble: Arun Kumar Sahoo @ vs State Of Odisha .... Opp. Parties on 24 August, 2021 Author: S.K. Sahoo Bench: S.K. Sahoo In The High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack Blapl No.1664 of 2021 1. Arun Kumar Sahoo @ Rinku 2. Bikranta Sahoo @ Ricky .... Petitioners Mr. A. Tripathy, Advocate -versus- State of Odisha .... Opp. Parties Mr. S.S. Pradhan, Addl. Government Advocate Coram: Justice S.K. Sahoo Order Order No. 24.08.2021 04.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the samples were collected during the course of raid conducted on 22.12.2020 by the I.I.C., Badambadi police station and his team in the Tomato Sauce manufacturing unit situated at Netaji Nagar near Hanuman Temple, Cuttack and the chemical examination report indicates that all the items conformed to the prescribed standards under the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 and only the samples required proper labeling as per Food Safety and Standards (Packing and Labelling) Regulations, 2011. He further submitted that the Arun Kumar Sahoo @ vs State Of Odisha .... Opp. Parties on 24 August, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2293072/ 1 one Bulu Sahoo is the tenant of the house in which the preparation of the food products was going on and the petitioners are the workers and they have been falsely entangled in this case and they are in judicial custody since 22.12.2020 and therefore, the bail application of the petitioners may be favourably considered. Learned counsel for the State, on the other hand, submitted that the petitioners are nephews of the tenant Bulu Sahoo, who was found absent when the raid was conducted and the petitioners were present in the house in question. Learned counsel for the State also filed a report of the Food Analyst of the Government of Odisha, which indicates that the samples of Soya Sauce, Chilli Sauce, Tomato Sauce, // 3 // Masala Powder, Dal Tadka, Coriander Powder, Cumin Powder conformed to the prescribed standard under the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 based on the test performed, but the samples required proper labeling as per Food Safety and Standards (Packing and Labelling) Regulations, 2011 and so far as the colour is concerned, the sample is a non-permitted food colour. It is further stated that as per the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006, Rules and Regulations, 2011, absence of batch number and details of manufacturing/packaging is in violation of the Packing and Labelling Regulations, 2011 and the same comes under mis-branded category.
